title: Book Three · Chapter 128: The First Six Yuan
story:
On Friday, a woman brings a small drawing to the workshop.

She wants a shelf for cups above her kitchen table. Mr Sun is finishing a check at the back, so Ronan meets her at the counter.

She puts the drawing down.

“This long. But not very deep.”

Ronan finds a clean sheet. He copies the length, then looks at the cups in her little picture.

“How many cups?”

“Six.”

“All the same size?”

She smiles. “Not in my kitchen.”

He draws one large circle and several small ones. The woman moves her finger between them.

“The big one has a handle too.”

Ronan adds the handle. Then he asks if she can bring that cup or its size.

“I can bring it tomorrow.”

She touches the drawing again.

“I forgot about the handle when I did that.”

Ronan looks at his large circle. A cup on paper is easy to make smaller. The cup in her kitchen will keep its own size.

“Do they stand in a row?”

“Most of the time.”

She moves his clean sheet beside her own. With one finger, she shows him the place for the largest cup.

Ronan draws the little handle on that side too. He leaves room around it.

“Like that?”

“Yes. I need to take it down easily.”

He almost writes a size beside the circles. Then he looks at her empty hands. Neither of them has the cup here yet.

He moves his pencil to the words instead. He writes largest cup beside the question and reads it back to her.

She nods. Her finger stays beside the place she has chosen until he finishes the line.

Mr Sun comes to the counter. Ronan shows him the length and the question about depth. He has left that space blank.

Mr Sun looks at the drawing and talks to the woman. They agree to check her largest cup before he gives the final size and price.

After she leaves, he turns the paper toward Ronan.

“That question helped.”

“The handle?”

“The cup itself.”

Ronan smiles and puts the sheet with her name.

At twelve, Mr Sun checks the week: Monday, Wednesday, Friday. Ronan has worked all three mornings, nine until twelve.

Mr Sun gives him six yuan.

Ronan counts it and writes the date on an envelope. He puts the money inside while Mr Sun closes the book.

“Monday again,” Mr Sun says.

“Monday.”

Ronan goes out with the envelope in his pocket. Dad stays to finish his own working day.

At the food stall near home, Ronan buys a small bag of peanuts for one yuan. He pays from the new six and puts the remaining five back in the envelope.

Mum is with a customer when he comes in. He leaves the peanuts on the kitchen table and waits in the yard until she finishes.

Then he shows her the envelope.

“First week.”

She looks at the date and smiles.

“And the kitchen?”

“One yuan.”

She takes a peanut and cracks it open.

That evening, Dad takes one too. Ronan tells them about the largest cup and its handle.

Mum looks at Dad's tea cup. Its handle is wide, and there is a small crack near the bottom.

“Use mine for the next drawing,” Dad says.

Ronan laughs and passes him the bag. He leaves five yuan in the work envelope and puts it beside his own books before dinner.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

depth＝深度；blank＝空白的；peanut＝花生；crack＝裂痕，也可指把壳掰开。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan问了哪个具体问题，让这张架子需求更清楚？他有没有自行报最终价格？
2. 第一周实得多少钱？花生花了多少？新工资信封还剩多少？

## 读句子

**He has left that space blank.**

拆开看：He / has left / that space / blank.

他／让……保持着／那一栏／空白。
